title: Never feeling part of the jazz scene
summary: He felt outside jazz because the written note was undesirable.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: I want to ask you about a statement you made to me a few days ago. You said something to the effect that you really felt that you hadn't been part of the "jazz scene"--
Do you think that's true throughout your career or--
Yes. I always felt like that.
Even when you were writing for Norvo or Goodman?
Or writing for jazz musicians? Why do you feel like that?
I don't know, maybe because I was always made to feel that the written note was somehow not desirable.
Yes. We are always writing pretty much (inaudible). I got around that by studying alot and by taking lessons. I was just as baffled by people like Bartok and Stravinsky; how did they do it? How
can it be that someone could be that good? I felt that way about performing jazz musicians too.
Don't you think the problem you describe is one that any arranger who is a composer and/or arranger who has worked in the jazz field?
